checked_classes: Ordering errors: tasks 1–6 precede executable scenario authoring, final compilation/builds/manifests, and G1/G2; failure corrections refresh affected artifact bindings before rerunning the failed gate.

Missing dependencies: the manifest contains an acyclic dependency graph covering contract implementation, caller migration, provider/catalog work, integration preparation, execution, correction, and independent review.

Untestable acceptance criteria: FC-UAR-PERSISTENCE and FC-POSTACK-CANCEL explicitly identify unresolved controls, require genuine execution oracles, and mandate BLOCKED/unrun dispositions that prevent acceptance.

Ambiguous acceptance criteria: eager/deferred source-specific counts, strict authority refusals, consumption ordering, uncertainty, restart behavior, and retained projection assertions have stated oracles and evidence boundaries.

Scope smuggling: planned production changes stay within the approved native lifecycle and provider discovery amendment; additional paths and production instrumentation require explicit scope handling.

Constraint violations: Plan prohibits product execution, preserves dirty-source inventories and excluded D0 paths, and prohibits replacement executors, production debug switches, dependency upgrades, publication, and parent certification.
Ownership conflicts: overlapping Boss paths retain one owner, integration authors receive ownership only after production writers finish, and root serializes builds and gates.

Unsupported causal or verification claims: runtime12 causation remains unknown, commands are declarations rather than receipts, and acceptance requires fresh source-bound artifacts and actual gate outcomes.
Lifecycle boundary violations: Execute requires operator approval; Reflect, child exit, archive, and parent decisions remain separate later gates.
